title: Vigia Mais MT facial recognition identifies a woman wanted for drug trafficking in downtown Cuiabá; Ciosp tracks her in real time and the 1st Military Police Battalion arrests her
summary: Mato Grosso's security secretariat reports that Vigia Mais MT facial recognition matched a woman wanted for drug trafficking in central Cuiabá on 12 July 2025, and police arrested her.
account: On 19 June 2024 the 9th Criminal Court Specialized in Drug Offenses issued a warrant for a woman for drug trafficking. On Saturday 12 July 2025 the video-monitoring system of Mato Grosso's State Secretariat of Public Security (Sesp) helped arrest her in downtown Cuiabá. It acted through the Vigia Mais MT program. Cameras in the city center identified her by facial recognition. After the system confirmed her identity, the monitoring center of the Integrated Public Security Operations Center (Ciosp) tracked her movements in real time. The center passed them to a team of the 1st Military Police Battalion, which made the approach. She was taken to a Civil Judicial Police unit. On 14 July 2025 Maria Klara Duque wrote a release about the arrest for the secretariat. Diário de Cuiabá and O Documento carried the text of that release on 14 July, and CliqueF5 carried it on 15 July 2025. Diário de Cuiabá and CliqueF5 credit it to the secretariat. The reports add that from April to July 2025 about 60 fugitives were located and arrested by state security forces. The release adds that the Vigia Mais MT program then covered 128 municipalities.
purpose: Vigia Mais MT is the state's video-monitoring program. Its facial recognition compares faces seen on public cameras with wanted persons so that Ciosp can direct patrols to them. Locating a person with an open warrant is that purpose.
system: Vigia Mais MT video-monitoring facial recognition (Sesp-MT / Ciosp)
deployer: Secretaria de Estado de Segurança Pública de Mato Grosso (Sesp-MT), through the Centro Integrado de Operações de Segurança Pública (Ciosp)
segment: Public-space facial recognition against warrant lists

ratings.reason: Sesp-MT's Ciosp located a woman wanted since a 19 June 2024 warrant and tracked her in real time, per the 14 July 2025 reports. It handed her to the 1st Military Police Battalion, which arrested her. A measurable result for the unit.
One person with an open drug-trafficking warrant was taken into custody. The reports give no evidence of any further harm prevented. So the public benefit is the execution of a warrant.

ai_role.statement: The reports credit the facial recognition system with the identification. Cameras in central Cuiabá matched her face and the system confirmed her identity. Ciosp operators then tracked her and a Military Police team made the arrest. The sources do not name the vendor, the algorithm or any match score. They come from a single text that reads as the state's release.

display.answer: All three news reports carry the text of a release that Maria Klara Duque wrote for the Mato Grosso security secretariat on 14 July 2025, and the record cites that release. The OECD Monitor entry of 14 July 2025 describes the same arrest.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: Mato Grosso's security secretariat reports that Vigia Mais MT facial recognition matched a woman wanted for drug trafficking in central Cuiabá on 12 July 2025, and police arrested her.
fields.account: On 19 June 2024 the 9th Criminal Court Specialized in Drug Offenses issued a warrant for a woman for drug trafficking. On Saturday 12 July 2025 the video-monitoring system of Mato Grosso's State Secretariat of Public Security (Sesp) helped arrest her in downtown Cuiabá. It acted through the Vigia Mais MT program. Cameras in the city center identified her by facial recognition. After the system confirmed her identity, the monitoring center of the Integrated Public Security Operations Center (Ciosp) tracked her movements in real time. The center passed them to a team of the 1st Military Police Battalion, which made the approach. She was taken to a Civil Judicial Police unit. On 14 July 2025 Maria Klara Duque wrote a release about the arrest for the secretariat. Diário de Cuiabá and O Documento carried the text of that release on 14 July, and CliqueF5 carried it on 15 July 2025. Diário de Cuiabá and CliqueF5 credit it to the secretariat. The reports add that from April to July 2025 about 60 fugitives were located and arrested by state security forces. The release adds that the Vigia Mais MT program then covered 128 municipalities.
